s14_archaeology_correction.defect: I obtained the 12 by filtering world NAMES beginning 'A2-'. World names are author-supplied metadata, which is exactly what an archaeologist is not entitled to trust. I used the author's intent to prove the author's intent was recoverable.
s14_archaeology_correction.corrected: substrate-only, the frozen R_SPEC rule returns 64 worlds for the A2 analysis, precision 0.09. It does NOT isolate A2 in this store.
s14_archaeology_correction.why: every S14 attack used the same bare default spec, so spec_hash collapsed 64 worlds into one group. S13's constructions each carried a distinguishing spec, which is why R_SPEC scored 1.00/0.85 there.
s14_archaeology_correction.qualification_of_TB: R_SPEC's precision is a function of SPEC DISCIPLINE, which is claimant-controlled. A claimant who uses generic specs degrades the derived universe into uselessness -- so spec_hash is a fixed point against an adversary who VARIES the spec, but not against one who makes every spec identical.
s14_archaeology_correction.open_not_result: a spec+time composite may separate A2 (its worlds occupy a contiguous 1.1s window containing 0 others), but that rule was not pre-registered and inventing it after seeing which attack needs it is the prohibited move. Requires fresh pre-registration.
